_comment: SCOPE OF THIS FILE — verified against production 2026-07-22.
The Azure Static Web Apps Next.js hybrid adapter honours only PART of this schema.
WORKS:    routes[].redirect  — the /about, /solutions and /contact entries below
return real 301s in production. Do not move these to next.config.js.
IGNORED:  globalHeaders, routes[].headers, responseOverrides. All three were present
and silently had no effect; the site served zero security headers as a
result. They have been removed rather than left as a decoy.
IGNORED:  platform.apiRuntime — proven inert 2026-07-29 by three preview deploys:
apiRuntime node:22 + build 20 gave runtime 20; node:22 + build 22 gave 22;
node:20 + build 22 ALSO gave 22. The hybrid runtime Node version comes
solely from NODE_VERSION in cost-optimized-ci.yml (the Oryx build version).
Removed rather than left as a decoy, same as the header keys above. Do not
re-add it expecting it to pin the runtime; change NODE_VERSION instead.
Response headers (CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy)
are now served from next.config.js headers(). Edit them there, not here.
LOCALE REDIRECTS: /en /es /fr and their five sub-pages 301 to the canonical
English path. next-intl is installed but never wired up, so every locale served
identical English at 200 (duplicate content). These use routes[].redirect — the
same mechanism proven to work above — NOT next.config.js redirects(), which the
hybrid adapter ignores and which broke the entire route map when tried 2026-07-23.
